author: Mara A. Mulrooney, Andrew McAlister, Christopher M. Stevenson, Alex E. Morrison and Lissa Gendreau
title: Sourcing Rapa Nui Mata‘a from the Collections of Bishop Museum Using Non-Destructive pXRF. Journal of the Polynesian Society 123(3), 301–338 (2014)
reference: Sourcing Rapa Nui Mata‘a from the Collections of Bishop Museum Using Non-Destructive pXRF. Journal of the Polynesian Society 123(3), 301–338 (2014). https://doi.org/10.15286/jps.123.3.301-338

notes.text:
A privately supplied PDF was used for transcription. Its SHA-256 is 31157ea92bccf67883170f34abd6ca2d31de3c5665051816ff1b5ae63512ef8c; its original retrieval date is unknown. Permission to share the PDF has not been granted, so no capture is registered. PDF, page renders and raw OCR remain private.

The paper reports 332 analysed mata‘a (302 complete and 30 broken) on printed p. 303. The appendix, printed pp. 324–334, has 332 distinct Sample No. labels, transcribed visually with OCR used only to locate rows. Page row counts are 29, 32, 29, 32, 30, 32, 29, 32, 29, 32 and 26. Repeated B3481 letter suffixes, including lowercase ell, were visually distinguished. These analytical specimen labels do not by themselves establish current catalogue identities. The acquisition counts on printed p. 304 sum to 333 (232 + 81 + 20); the difference from the analysed sample and appendix is unexplained.

C8353 is explicitly called an accession number on printed p. 314. B3481c and B3481bbbb are paper Sample Nos.; neither is independently verified as a museum accession. Their separate rows (appendix p. 325) and joint discussion (p. 317) support keeping them distinct. The extracted descriptions preserve the paper's wording, including analytical disagreement and uncertainty; geological source assignments do not establish manufacturing or find locations. The paper does not establish present custody.
